g.title: cluster_legend
g.text: Legend — solid: owns · dark: relationship · dashed: reference

a.xlink:title: Define and verify an opinionated DDD framework for modeling systems, tracing guarantees, and controlling change impact.
Own the workflow for creating, reviewing, revising, and retiring model nodes.
Own human-readable model views, explanations, and citations without owning structural model facts.
Define the kinds of nodes and edges that can exist in a ddduck model.
Own the executable tools that validate, assemble, and generate artifacts from the canonical model.
Own the rules that prove model completeness, coherence, and guarantee lifecycle coverage.
Own generated exports that adapt canonical model data for external visualization tools.
Capture durable architectural decisions and link them back to model nodes.
Govern how model nodes are introduced, changed, stabilized, deprecated, and retired.
Authoring Workflow creates and updates model nodes whose allowed kinds and edge rules are defined by Metamodel.
Indicate whether a documentation view reflects the current canonical model state.
Present model knowledge in human-readable prose, tables, diagrams, or generated pages.
Cite a canonical model, domain, concept, relationship, decision, or rule ID from documentation.
State a documentation assertion about model structure, ownership, relationships, decisions, or verification policy.
Represent a documentation view whose structural claims are generated from or checked against canonical model nodes.
Documentation reads canonical model node definitions when explaining structure, ownership, and relationships.
Represent a single authoritative model element stored as canonical YAML.
Name a domain-owned idea that may later become a richer model node.
Define an ownership boundary inside a model.
Represent an integrated context whose rules are not owned by this model.
Describe a whole system and contain its owned domains and relationships.
Define the recognized kind of a canonical model node.
Connect domains or model nodes through explicit typed references.
Define when tooling commands may write human-readable output to stdout or stderr.
Represent an executable aggregate check that must pass before accepting canonical changes.
Tooling Runtime executes traceability checks and reports validation results for the canonical model.
Decide whether required model and guarantee coverage is sufficient for a change.
Identify a model reference whose target node or decision cannot be resolved.
Record the lifecycle state or handling outcome of a guarantee, rule, or finding.
Preserve stable representation and reproducible diffs as a model and documentation policy.
State an expected property that traceability rules must preserve or verify.
Record traceability evidence, coverage, or change impact in an auditable form.
Detect a policy, consistency, or model-coherence violation.
Identify a model node that is not reachable from the expected ownership or graph roots.
Describe a canonical YAML policy rule that executable tooling can enforce.
Prove that a model node conforms to its declared JSON Schema.
Traceability validates that documentation references resolve and that verified views stay aligned with canonical model facts.
Traceability validates that model nodes and edges defined under Metamodel resolve and remain coherent.
Represent the generated ContextFlow project artifact used for temporary visualization exports.
Visualization Export reads canonical model topology and emits derived graph artifacts such as ContextFlow project JSON.
